page: Amazon Web Services c5a.16xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor and driven by a 3.3 GHz AMD EPYC 7R32 processor. Featuring an x86_64 architecture, this virtual machine supplies 64 vCPUs across 32 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The instance is paired with 128 GB of DDR4 system memory running at 3 GHz, providing a standardized 1:2 compute-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per core. It operates with a 20 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, includes no bundled local NVMe storage, and contains no discrete graphics accelerators.

Benchmark data reveals robust multi-threaded processing and cryptographic throughput, with PassMark CPU, extended instructions, and encryption scores placing in the top quartile. Geekbench ray tracing performance similarly ranks in the top 25 percent. Conversely, single-core processing capabilities reflect noticeable constraints, with stress-ng single-core metrics placing in the bottom 10 percent and large-parameter language model generation falling into the bottom quartile. Memory bandwidth remains balanced, delivering 115.92 GB/sec on large uncached read operations.

From a resource efficiency perspective, the AMD-based hardware configuration delivers high multi-core compute density, making it cost-efficient for parallelized workloads that do not require expansive per-core memory or dedicated hardware acceleration. The absence of local disk requires external volume attachments, which constitutes a primary architecture tradeoff.

The c5a.16xlarge is well tailored for distributed compute workloads, software compilation via multi-threaded toolchains, batch processing pipelines, video rendering, and concurrent web serving infrastructures.
description: Amazon Web Services c5a.16xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server powered by a 32-core AMD EPYC 7R32 processor delivering 64 vCPUs at 3.3 GHz on the Nitro hypervisor. Configured with 128 GB of DDR4 memory at a 2.0 GB per core ratio and a 20 Gbps baseline network capacity, this instance features no integrated local storage or GPU hardware. Performance benchmarks highlight strong multi-core computational and cryptographic throughput, ranking in the top 25 percent in PassMark CPU and encryption tests alongside Geekbench ray tracing. However, single-core throughput is limited, as evidenced by bottom-tier stress-ng results and modest large-scale LLM generation speeds. Delivering dense multi-core processing without the overhead of massive memory footprints, the c5a.16xlarge serves compute-intensive tasks, parallel CI/CD compilation, batch transformations, and high-concurrency web serving.
